info.name: JazzWorld AI Impact Awards Portal
info.description:
# AI Awards Portal

OpenShift `ocpv2` / namespace `people-org`

## Read this first

This is a **server-rendered Next.js application, not a REST API**. There are exactly **three** conventional HTTP endpoints:

| Endpoint | Auth |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/health` | none |
| `GET /admin/export/submissions` | admin |
| `GET /admin/export/evaluations` | admin |

Everything else is a **page** (GET, returns HTML) or a **server action** (POST to a page URL). Both are covered, and anything that cannot be driven from Postman says so on the request.

## Sign-in flow

No passwords, no API keys - email one-time code.

```
/  (public landing)  ->  click Submit an initiative
                     ->  /login          request code
                     ->  /login/verify   enter 6-digit code
                     ->  /submit         (nominee lands here)
```

1. Set `{{loginEmail}}` to a mailbox you can read
2. Run **2. Auth / 1. Request sign-in code**
3. Read the code, set `{{otpCode}}`
4. Run **2. Auth / 2. Verify code** - Postman stores `aia_session` and reuses it

Sessions last **8 hours** and are revoked server-side on sign out. Only `jazz.com.pk` / `jazz.com` addresses may sign in.

## Roles

| Role | Lands on | Can |
|---|---|---|
| nominee | `/submit` | submit a nomination |
| reviewer | `/committee/queue` | score submissions |
| approver | `/admin` | see aggregates, approve / disapprove |
| admin | `/admin` | everything except approving |

## Rate limits will stop an automated run

3 codes per address / 15 min - 12 per IP / 15 min - **5 distinct addresses per IP / hour**. Deliberate: it closes ISG finding IDX-001.

item.name: 2. Auth (email OTP)
item.description: Run 1 then 2. The session cookie is stored automatically.

request.description: Public. Renders the email form and carries the action id.

**Server action, not a REST endpoint.** Next.js App Router exposes these as POSTs to the page URL, identified by a hidden `$ACTION_ID_<hash>` field that is **build-scoped** - it changes every deploy. The pre-request script reads the current value into `{{actionId}}`.

The body **must be `multipart/form-data`**. A urlencoded POST does not invoke the action - it is served as an ordinary page request, which can look like a pass when nothing ran.

Emails a 6-digit code. On success redirects to `/login/verify`; otherwise back to `/login?e=...`:

| `e=` | meaning |
|---|---|
| `domain` | address outside the allowed domains |
| `rate` | 3-per-address limit hit |
| `iprate` | 5-addresses-per-device limit hit |
| `send` | SMTP relay unreachable |

request.description: Requires a session; anonymous visitors are redirected to `/login`.

**Server action, not a REST endpoint.** Next.js App Router exposes these as POSTs to the page URL, identified by a hidden `$ACTION_ID_<hash>` field that is **build-scoped** - it changes every deploy. The pre-request script reads the current value into `{{actionId}}`.

The body **must be `multipart/form-data`**. A urlencoded POST does not invoke the action - it is served as an ordinary page request, which can look like a pass when nothing ran.

**Requires a session** - the action authorises itself, not merely via the page guard (ISG IDX-005 follow-up). `submitterEmail` must be an allowed domain or it is rejected with `303 /submit?e=domain` (VULN-004).

Success: `303 -> /status/<new id>`. Submissions are attributed to the signed-in user.

File attachments are omitted here - object storage is currently blocked by egress policy.

### Team members (Section 2)

`submissionType` is `Individual` or `Team`. Team members are **parallel repeated fields** — send `teamMemberName` and `teamMemberContribution` once per row, in matching order; the server zips them and drops any row with a blank name.

Contribution must be one of `Ideation`, `Development`, `Ideation and Development` — anything else is discarded server-side.

With `submissionType=Individual` the list is stored as `[]` **regardless of what you post**, so the rows above are ignored in that case.

This replaces the former single `teamMembers` free-text field. Submissions filed before the change still hold that string and continue to render.

item.name: 6. Admin / Approver
item.description: `/admin` is open to admin and approver. Everything else is admin-only.

request.description:
Panel averages, evaluator x criterion matrix, evaluator notes and approval decisions. Paginated, 25 per page (`?page=2`).

Approvers see the same view plus an Approve / Disapprove control; admins see the decisions but cannot approve.
**Admin only.** Approvers are redirected.
**Admin only.** Real route handler. `text/csv`, includes panel averages.
**Admin only.** Real route handler. `text/csv`, one row per evaluation.

**Server action, not a REST endpoint.** Next.js App Router exposes these as POSTs to the page URL, identified by a hidden `$ACTION_ID_<hash>` field that is **build-scoped** - it changes every deploy. The pre-request script reads the current value into `{{actionId}}`.

The body **must be `multipart/form-data`**. A urlencoded POST does not invoke the action - it is served as an ordinary page request, which can look like a pass when nothing ran.

**Approver role only.** One decision per approver per submission - re-submitting revises it rather than adding a row (enforced by a unique index).

`decision` must be `approved` or `disapproved`. This never changes the panel score or the lifecycle status.

request.description:
Informational. Sign in, then decode the `aia_session` cookie at jwt.io: `exp - iat` must be **28800 seconds (8h)**. It was 604800 (7 days) at the time of the report.

The token also carries a `jti`, which is what makes server-side revocation possible.
